ideas.pitch: A localized energy grid forecasting tool tailored for Upstate New York municipalities to predict peak load and renewable output anomalies using Poisson regression and geospatial satellite monitoring.
ideas.title: TroyGrid AI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines rigorous forecasting with localized regional utility relevance, matching the technical depth seen in winning statistical and satellite monitoring projects.

ideas.pitch: An AI-powered multi-agent student support and sustainability tracker that coordinates campus resource allocation and carbon footprint reduction initiatives using LangGraph and localized RAG.
ideas.title: CampusGreen Multi-Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly mirrors the winning multi-agent student platform architecture while targeting a universally appealing university campus improvement use case.

ideas.pitch: An AML risk detection and investigation dashboard utilizing graph intelligence and explainable gradient boosting to map and flag suspicious transaction networks for local financial cooperatives.
ideas.title: Hudson AML Inspector
ideas.why_it_could_win: Employs genuine hard engineering through graph intelligence and explainable machine learning models, replicating the winning formula of top fintech hackathon entries.

ideas.pitch: An AI-driven regional nutritional assistant that generates personalized meal recommendations and sourcing routes based on inventory from local Upstate New York farmers markets and co-ops.
ideas.title: LocalHarvest Nutrition Engine
ideas.why_it_could_win: Takes the proven winner template of personalized nutrition platforms and grounds it in hyper-local community economics, which local hackathon judges favor.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous AI agent marketplace facilitating micro-task execution and instant USDC escrow payments tailored for student freelance and research compute sharing.
ideas.title: RPI Autonomous Escrow Dispatch
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the proven winning pattern of autonomous agent marketplaces paired with cryptographic escrow rails, appealing to judges interested in decentralized automation.
